lead.t: Thyroid storm – an acute, life‑threatening decompensation of hyperthyroidism characterised by multisystem hypermetabolism, usually precipitated by a stressor in a patient with untreated or inadequately treated Graves’ disease or toxic nodular goitre.

b: Description : A life-threatening crisis of acute hyperthyroidism where symptoms are significantly heightened.
Causes : Can be triggered by surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, uncontrolled diabetes, stress, abrupt withdrawal of antithyroid medications, or other precipitating events.

qs.e: Thyroid storm: hyperpyrexia, tachycardia/arrhythmias, agitation, vomiting, high-output cardiac failure. Mortality ~20–30%. Treatment: propylthiouracil (blocks synthesis AND T4→T3 conversion) + Lugol's iodine + propranolol + steroids + supportive care.
